errors.english: Should not be despised in this world,
errors.why: The verse says the person should do what is not censured in this world (and brings happiness in the next); 'not censured' qualifies the action, not the person.

fix.find: Should not be despised in this world,
fix.replace: Should do what is not censured in this world,

note: Sound rendering of the buffalo-sacrifice and butcher's-son exempla and of the pride verse; one verse misconstrued.

errors.english: it would result in an infinite regress (prasanga) reductio ad absurdum
errors.why: ha cang thal ba is atiprasaṅga, an absurd overextension; the infinite regress (thug pa med pa) is a separate step argued afterwards.

fix.find: it would result in an infinite regress (prasanga) reductio ad absurdum
fix.replace: it would be an absurd overextension (atiprasaṅga)

errors.english: it is impossible for them to possess number, because both [note: universals and numbers], being qualitative entities,
errors.why: grangs dang ldan pa is 'number and conjunction' (saṃkhyā and saṃyoga), the two Vaiśeṣika qualities that reside only in substances; universals are not qualities, so the note is wrong.

fix.find: it is impossible for them to possess number, because both [note: universals and numbers], being qualitative entities,
fix.replace: neither number nor conjunction (saṃyoga) is possible for them, because both, being qualities (guṇa),

errors.english: space itself has no distinct parts
errors.why: The conclusion is that space is not different from its 'nature' (no distinction between the two), not that space lacks parts.

note: The Vaiśeṣika argument is followed, but two technical terms (atiprasaṅga, number-and-conjunction) are mistranslated.

errors.english: When it arises in men who wish for harm,
errors.why: The anger arises in oneself, and it is the ill-wishers who rejoice when it does; it does not arise in them.

errors.english: Then by abandoning it, a bad reputation arises
errors.why: The verse (contrasting with the next, where one who treats anger as an enemy gains fame like the waxing moon) says ill repute befalls the one who harbours heart-burning anger, his fame fading like the moon at dawn, not the one who abandons it.

errors.english: [note: original: "gtam ngan" — here implying the loss of a worldly, aggressive reputation in favor of peace]
errors.why: The note rationalises the misreading; gtam ngan is plain disrepute incurred through anger.

note: Narrative frame is good, but the anger verses are partly misconstrued, inverting one stanza's moral.

errors.english: Previously, this commentary was set forth
errors.why: rnam 'grel here is the Vārttika (the root verse being commented on), not 'this commentary'.

errors.english: it is because there is no unerring deviation (avyabhicāra) invariable concomitance
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'because there is non-deviation (avyabhicāra)'; 'no unerring deviation' garbles it into near-nonsense.

note: Accurate on tādātmya/tadutpatti and saṃyoga as reasons; two term slips.
Faithful rendering of the apoha discussion and of the isolated-word (prameya) argument.

errors.english: How could those, through that very way, namely through their nature, arise from a specific natural quality?
errors.why: For natural things it is legitimate to argue by their nature: 'as it arises from a specific nature there, why not here too?'; the English turns the premise into a sceptical rhetorical question.

errors.english: refering to the mental continuum of the practitioner
errors.why: The continuum transformed by the application is that of the (momentary) mantra itself, whose successive moments are given special qualities, not the practitioner's mind.

note: Mīmāṃsā mantra-efficacy argument is mostly followed; one inference garbled and a misleading note.

errors.english: through the force of strong attachment
errors.why: lhag par zhen pa in pramāṇa is adhyavasāya, determination (conceptual ascertainment), not attachment.

fix.find: through the force of strong attachment

note: Clear and accurate on conceptual cognition and the vyavahartṛ's conflation; one key term wrong.

errors.english: if the two parties—the proponent and the opponent—fail to establish or feel doubt regarding the subject to be understood or the means of understanding, it is problematic
errors.why: go bar bya ba / go bar byed pa are the two persons (pratipādya, the one to be convinced, and pratipādaka, the one who convinces): 'even when stated, if it is unestablished or doubtful for the two', not a subject and a means of understanding.

fix.find: if the two parties—the proponent and the opponent—fail to establish or feel doubt regarding the subject to be understood or the means of understanding, it is problematic
fix.replace: even when it is stated, if it is unestablished or doubtful for the two parties, the one to be convinced (pratipādya) and the one who convinces (pratipādaka), it is likewise a fallacy

note: Good on the asiddha examples (visibility of sound, Digambara tree argument); the Nyāyabindu quotation is misconstrued.

errors.english: the Tathagata [note: The Buddha] caused his body to be illuminated with supreme clarity. Out of devotion, he performed the funeral rites
errors.why: 'Supreme illuminator' is an epithet of the Tathāgata, who out of devotion worshipped the king's body; he did not make the body shine.

fix.find: the Tathagata [note: The Buddha] caused his body to be illuminated with supreme clarity. Out of devotion, he performed the funeral rites
fix.replace: the Tathagata [note: The Buddha], the supreme illuminator, out of devotion worshipped his body

errors.english: The one who serves the feet of the Great One is sustained in this world and the next
errors.why: The line says '(that dawn) is worthy of praise among days'; this is not rendered, and 'serves the feet... is sustained' stands in its place.

note: Tibetan portions of the bilingual side are translated (Sanskrit lines duplicate them); the Śuddhodana funeral verse is misconstrued.
Both the Sanskrit and the Tibetan of the colophon and the Sāketa opening verses are rendered faithfully and kept distinct.
